hero.bio: I'm a backend-leaning full-stack developer who takes systems apart to see the wiring. Mostly product engineering for real businesses — sometimes real-time games, sometimes a hackathon algorithm at 2am that only had to work once.
hero.terminalCurrently: shipping EduCore, chasing the next podium

about.headline: Every bug starts the same way:
about.bio1: I got into this by breaking things — a Java desktop app for a hotel that had to survive real receptionists, a real-time game that had to survive real players cheating the clock. Fixing what I'd broken taught me more than any course did.
about.bio2: These days that looks like backend services at a bank by day, and hackathons, side projects and certifications by night. I care about the parts most people skip: the edge case, the failed migration, the first ten seconds of using something new.

beyond.headline: Six things that keep me at the keyboard longer than planned.

studies.title: Teaching a bot to besiege
studies.description: A depth-limited minimax opponent for a real-time territory game — tuned to be good enough to lose to on purpose.

studies.title: The shape I keep drawing
studies.description: Three intersecting bars, eighteen faces, drawn as solids with their edges kept. Rotation and dolly are bound to this scrollbar.

studies.title: State, kept honest
studies.description: Socket rooms with a chess-clock timer per player — the hard part was never the game, it was the reconnect.

studies.title: Freed rooms, refilled fast
studies.description: A small heuristic that re-ranks the waiting list the moment a room opens, instead of first-come-first-served.
